source.text: וְאֵ֤לֶּה הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִנִּ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יָדְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־מִלְחֲמ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the nations that left Yahweh to test by them Israel, all who not had known all [the] wars of Canaan,

en.L: And these [are] the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} left, to test Israel by them, all who had not known any of the wars of Canaan,
en.B: These are the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} left in the land to test Israel by them, that is, all those in Israel who had never known any of the wars for Canaan.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} left some nations in the land. He used them to test the Israelites who had never fought in the wars to win Canaan.

decisions.choice: God left these nations in the land on purpose, as a test
decisions.reason: Because Israel broke the covenant, God said he would no longer drive out the nations Joshua left, but would use them to test whether Israel would keep his way (2:20-23). Verse 4 states the test again.

decisions.choice: had not known the wars of Canaan: had no experience of the fighting by which the land was taken
decisions.reason: "Know" here means to know by experience. These are the generation that grew up after Joshua and did not see what the LORD had done for Israel (2:10).

decisions.choice: He used them to test
decisions.reason: Readable splits the sentence in two and makes the purpose a sentence of its own, with God as the one who tests.

source.text: רַ֗ק לְמַ֨עַן֙ דַּ֚עַת דֹּר֣וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְלַמְּדָ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥ק אֲשֶׁר־לְפָנִ֖ים לֹ֥א יְדָעֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: only so as to know [the] generations of [the] sons of Israel, to teach them war, only those who before not had known them,

en.L: only so that the generations of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel might know [it], to teach them war, only those who had not known them before,
en.B: He did this only so that the generations of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would learn about war, at least those who had never experienced it before.
en.R: He did it so that each new generation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would learn how to fight, especially those who had never been in a battle.

decisions.choice: only ... only: the purpose is limited to teaching war to those who had no experience of it
decisions.reason: The word "only" comes twice. It narrows the purpose: the nations were left so that later generations, at least those who had not known war, would learn it. This stands beside the test of obedience in verses 1 and 4; the text does not say how the two purposes relate.

decisions.choice: to know ... to teach them war: to learn by experience how to fight
decisions.reason: "Know" again means experience, as in verse 1. A generation that never had to fight would now have to learn it with the nations still in the land.

decisions.choice: He did this
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the sentence of verse 1 with "only so that". Balanced and Readable start a new sentence and supply the subject and verb.

source.text: חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת׀סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וְכָל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַצִּ֣ידֹנִ֔י וְהַ֣חִוִּ֔י יֹשֵׁ֖ב הַ֣ר הַלְּבָנ֑וֹן מֵהַר֙ בַּ֣עַל חֶרְמ֔וֹן עַ֖ד לְב֥וֹא חֲמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: five rulers of [the] Philistines, and all the Canaanite[s], and the Sidonian[s], and the Hivite[s] dwelling [in the] mountain of the Lebanon, from [the] mountain of Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

en.L: the five rulers of [the] Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites living [in] the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
en.B: These were the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites and Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
en.R: They were the five Philistine rulers, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites. The Hivites lived in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon all the way to Lebo-hamath.

decisions.choice: rulers: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only of the Philistine leaders. Each ruled one of their five cities on the coastal plain: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (Joshua 13:3; 1 Samuel 6:17).

decisions.choice: Sidonians and Hivites: the peoples of the coast and mountains in the north
decisions.reason: The Sidonians were the people of Sidon and the Phoenician coast. The Hivites here live in the Lebanon range, so this list covers the southwest (the Philistines) and the far north, land Israel had not taken (Joshua 13:2-6).

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath: a town on the northern border
decisions.reason: The name can be read as a town, Lebo of Hamath, or as a phrase, "the entrance to Hamath". Both point to the same northern limit of the promised land (Numbers 34:8). Baal-hermon is probably Mount Hermon or a peak near it (1 Chronicles 5:23).

source.text: וַֽיִּהְי֕וּ לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָדַ֗עַת הֲיִשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה אֶת־אֲבוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they were to test by them Israel, to know whether they would hear [the] commandments of Yahweh which he commanded their fathers by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: And they were [there] to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
en.B: They were left to test Israel, to find out whether the Israelites would obey the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given their ancestors through Moses.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used these nations to test Israel. He wanted to see whether the Israelites would obey the commands {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given their ancestors through Moses.

decisions.choice: to test ... to know: to bring into the open what Israel would do
decisions.reason: God tests in order that what is in his people's hearts may be shown, not because he lacks knowledge (Deuteronomy 8:2; 13:4).

decisions.choice: listen to the commandments: obey them; by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: To "hear" a command is to obey it. "By the hand of" someone means through that person as God's agent.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the earlier generations of the people, women and men; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּקֶ֣רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Israel lived in [the] midst of the Canaanite[s], the Hittite[s], and the Amorite[s], and the Perizzite[s], and the Hivite[s], and the Jebusite[s].

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived right among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

decisions.choice: the six peoples of the land, now living side by side with Israel
decisions.reason: This is the list of the land's peoples from God's promise (Exodus 3:8; 23:23). Israel had been told to make no covenant with them (Deuteronomy 7:1-2), yet now Israel lives in their midst.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֨וּ אֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֤ם לָהֶם֙ לְנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נָתְנ֣וּ לִבְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and their daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.

en.L: And they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and their [own] daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.
en.B: They took the daughters of these peoples as wives, gave their own daughters to the sons of these peoples, and served their gods.
en.R: Israelite men took women from these nations as wives, and the Israelites gave their own daughters to men from these nations. They also worshiped the gods of these nations.

decisions.choice: marriage with the peoples of the land, leading to the worship of their gods
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 7:3-4 forbade exactly this, warning that such marriages would turn Israel's children away to serve other gods. The verse shows that warning coming true.

decisions.choice: served: worshiped
decisions.reason: To serve a god is to worship it and live under its claim.

decisions.choice: these peoples / these nations
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their" for both groups. Balanced and Readable name the other peoples so that it is clear whose daughters went where.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת־הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּשְׁכְּח֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] sons of Israel the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and forgot Yahweh their God, and served the Baals and the Asherahs.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and they served the Baals and the Asherahs.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. They forgot {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and worshiped the Baals and the goddesses called the Asherahs.

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: the formula that opens each round of the book's cycle
decisions.reason: The same words begin the story of each oppression (2:11; 3:12; 4:1; 6:1). What is evil is measured by what the LORD sees as evil.

decisions.choice: forgot: abandoned, ceased to be loyal to
decisions.reason: Forgetting God is not a lapse of memory but turning from him and his covenant (Deuteronomy 8:11-19).

decisions.choice: the Baals and the Asherahs: Canaanite gods and goddesses in their many local forms
decisions.reason: Baal was the storm god of Canaan, worshiped at many local shrines, so the plural speaks of these many forms. Asherah was a goddess, and the same word names the wooden poles set up for her (Exodus 34:13). Paired here with the Baals, the plural most likely means the goddess in her local forms or images. Judges 2:13 pairs Baal with the Ashtaroth instead.

decisions.choice: the Asherahs
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as a plural, since it stands beside the Baals as a group of deities; "Asherah poles" is kept for places where the objects are meant. Readable explains both names.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵ֗ם בְּיַד֙ כּוּשַׁ֣ן רִשְׁעָתַ֔יִם מֶ֖לֶךְ אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרָ֑יִם וַיַּעַבְד֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel, and he sold them into [the] hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and served [the] sons of Israel Cushan-rishathaim eight years.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into [the] hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
en.B: So the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sold them into the power of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
en.R: This made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} very angry with Israel. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to Cushan-rishathaim, the king of Aram-naharaim, a land far to the northeast. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had to serve him for eight years.

decisions.choice: the anger of Yahweh burned: God was very angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as a fire that flares up, as in 2:14 and 2:20.

decisions.choice: sold them into the hand of: handed them over to the power of
decisions.reason: As an owner sells a slave to a new master, God gives his people over to a foreign ruler (2:14; 4:2; 10:7). "Hand" stands for power.

decisions.choice: Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim: a ruler from the upper Euphrates
decisions.reason: Aram-naharaim, "Aram of the two rivers", is the land of the upper Euphrates in the far north, where Abraham's family lived (Genesis 24:10). The king is not known from any other source. His name can be heard as "Cushan of double wickedness", and the story may use it as a mocking name.

decisions.choice: a land far to the northeast
decisions.reason: Readable says where Aram-naharaim was, so the reader knows the oppressor came from far away.

decisions.choice: sold them into the power of / handed them over to
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of selling and says "power" for "hand"; Readable says plainly that God handed them over. This wording is used for the phrase throughout Judges.

source.text: וַיִּזְעֲק֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֥ה מוֹשִׁ֛יעַ לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיּֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑ם אֵ֚ת עָתְנִיאֵ֣ל בֶּן־קְנַ֔ז אֲחִ֥י כָלֵ֖ב הַקָּטֹ֥ן מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, and raised up Yahweh a deliverer for [the] sons of Israel, and he delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, [the] brother of Caleb, the younger than he.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up a deliverer for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and he delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, younger than he.
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up a deliverer for them, who rescued them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
en.R: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them someone to rescue them. It was Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.

decisions.choice: a deliverer: one who rescues from enemies
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from the same root, "save, rescue". This is the book's first description of the judges: people God raises to rescue Israel from oppressors (2:16, 18).

decisions.choice: younger than he: Othniel was Caleb's younger brother
alternatives: the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother (Othniel as Caleb's nephew)
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes Othniel as the younger brother. It could also be read as making Kenaz Caleb's younger brother, so that Othniel was Caleb's nephew. 1:13 and Joshua 15:17 use the same wording.

decisions.choice: Othniel: the hero who took Debir
decisions.reason: Othniel has already appeared in 1:12-13, where he captured Debir and married Caleb's daughter Achsah. The first judge comes from the family of Caleb, who followed the LORD fully (Numbers 14:24).

decisions.choice: for help
decisions.reason: Crying out to God here is a call for rescue. Readable says so.

source.text: וַתְּהִ֨י עָלָ֥יו רֽוּחַ־יְהוָה֮ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֵּצֵא֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַתָּ֣עָז יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was on him [the] Spirit of Yahweh, and he judged Israel, and he went out to war, and gave Yahweh into his hand Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram, and was strong his hand over Cushan-rishathaim.

en.L: And the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was on him, and he judged Israel, and he went out to war, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand was strong over Cushan-rishathaim.
en.B: The Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his power, so that he overpowered Cushan-rishathaim.
en.R: The Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Othniel, and he led Israel. He went out to fight, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave him victory over Cushan-rishathaim, the king of Aram. Othniel completely defeated him.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh came on him: God gave him power for his task
decisions.reason: This is the first time in the book that the Spirit comes on a judge. The Spirit gives the strength and leadership needed for rescue (6:34; 11:29; 14:6).

decisions.choice: judged Israel: led and governed Israel
decisions.reason: As at 2:16, a judge is a leader raised to rescue Israel and govern it, more than a judge in a court.

decisions.choice: gave into his hand ... his hand was strong over: God gave him the victory
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The LORD gives the enemy into Othniel's power, and so Othniel prevails.

decisions.choice: led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "led" for the verb "judge" throughout Judges, because "judge" suggests a court.

decisions.choice: Othniel
decisions.reason: Readable names Othniel where the Hebrew says "him" and "his".

source.text: וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֖רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּ֖מָת עָתְנִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־קְנַֽז׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And was quiet the land forty years, and died Othniel son of Kenaz.

en.L: And the land was quiet forty years. And Othniel son of Kenaz died.
en.B: Then the land had peace for forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
en.R: After that the land had peace for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.

decisions.choice: the land was quiet: it was at rest, free from war and oppression
decisions.reason: The verb means to be quiet or undisturbed. It closes each round of rescue (3:30; 5:31; 8:28).

decisions.choice: forty years: a full generation
decisions.reason: Forty is the usual span of a generation in the Bible (Numbers 14:33), and the book's periods of rest come in forties and eighties (5:31; 8:28; 3:30).

decisions.choice: had peace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the land had peace" for this formula throughout Judges; Literal keeps "was quiet".

source.text: וַיֹּסִ֨פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְחַזֵּ֨ק יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־עֶגְל֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָב֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֛ל כִּֽי־עָשׂ֥וּ אֶת־הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And again did [the] sons of Israel the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and strengthened Yahweh Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel again did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Once again the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Eglon king of Moab strong against Israel, because they had done what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Once again the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. Because of this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Eglon king of Moab strong enough to attack Israel.

decisions.choice: again: a new round of the cycle begins
decisions.reason: The verb means "to do again". After the rest of verse 11, Israel returns to the same evil as in verse 7, and the pattern starts over (4:1; 10:6; 13:1).

decisions.choice: Yahweh strengthened Eglon: God gave a foreign king power to discipline Israel
decisions.reason: The enemy's strength comes from the LORD, who uses Moab to punish his people's unfaithfulness, as 2:14-15 says. The verse names the reason twice.

decisions.choice: Eglon king of Moab: ruler of the land east of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Moab lay east of the Dead Sea; its people traced their descent from Lot (Genesis 19:37). Moab had tried to stop Israel on its way into the land (Numbers 22-24).

decisions.choice: Because of this
decisions.reason: Readable states the reason once, at the start of the second sentence, instead of repeating the whole phrase.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף אֵלָ֔יו אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת־עִ֥יר הַתְּמָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gathered to himself [the] sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and they took possession of [the] city of the palms.

en.L: And he gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the city of palms.
en.B: Eglon gathered the Ammonites and the Amalekites to join him, and he went and defeated Israel, and they took over the City of Palms.
en.R: He got the Ammonites and the Amalekites to join him. Then he attacked Israel and beat them, and they took over Jericho, the City of Palms.

decisions.choice: Ammon and Amalek: Moab's allies
decisions.reason: The Ammonites lived east of the Jordan, north of Moab. The Amalekites were desert raiders and old enemies of Israel (Exodus 17:8-16).

decisions.choice: the city of palms: Jericho
decisions.reason: Jericho, an oasis city in the Jordan valley, is called the city of palm trees in Deuteronomy 34:3 and 2 Chronicles 28:15. Jericho had been destroyed and placed under a curse (Joshua 6:26), so this was probably a settlement at its spring. From there Moab held the crossing into Israel's land.

decisions.choice: they took possession: Eglon and his allies
decisions.reason: The verb changes from "he" to "they": Eglon leads, and the combined force occupies the city.

decisions.choice: Jericho, the City of Palms
decisions.reason: Readable names the city the phrase refers to.

source.text: וַיַּעַבְד֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־עֶגְל֣וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָ֔ב שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And served [the] sons of Israel Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had to serve Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.

decisions.choice: served Eglon: lived as his subjects and paid him tribute
decisions.reason: Israel served the Baals (verse 7) and now must serve a foreign king. The tribute of verses 15-18 is part of that service. Eighteen years is more than twice the eight years under Cushan-rishathaim (verse 8).

source.text: וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ אֶל־יְהוָה֒ וַיָּקֶם֩ יְהוָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם מוֹשִׁ֗יעַ אֶת־אֵה֤וּד בֶּן־גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן־הַיְמִינִ֔י אִ֥ישׁ אִטֵּ֖ר יַד־יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּיָדוֹ֙ מִנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh, and raised up Yahweh for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a man restricted [in the] hand of his right; and sent [the] sons of Israel by his hand tribute to Eglon king of Moab.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up for them a deliverer, Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a man restricted [in] his right hand. And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, from the tribe of Benjamin, a left-handed man. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sent him to take their tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them someone to rescue them. This was Ehud son of Gera, from the tribe of Benjamin. Ehud was left-handed. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sent him to take the payment they owed to Eglon king of Moab.

decisions.choice: restricted in his right hand: left-handed
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a man who did not use his right hand, that is, a left-handed man. It may mean he was trained to fight with the left: 20:16 tells of 700 chosen left-handed men of Benjamin, and 1 Chronicles 12:2 of Benjaminites who used both hands. There is irony in the name: Benjamin means "son of the right hand".

decisions.choice: tribute: the payment owed by a subject people
decisions.reason: The word can mean a gift or a grain offering, but here it is the tribute a conquered people paid their overlord, in goods or silver (2 Samuel 8:2, where Moab pays tribute to David).

decisions.choice: by his hand: through him, with him as the one who carried it
decisions.reason: "By his hand" means Ehud was the agent who delivered the tribute.

decisions.choice: a left-handed man / Ehud was left-handed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the phrase. Literal keeps its form, "restricted in his right hand".

decisions.choice: the payment they owed
decisions.reason: "Tribute" is not a common word, so Readable explains it.

source.text: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ אֵה֜וּד חֶ֗רֶב וְלָ֛הּ שְׁנֵ֥י פֵי֖וֹת גֹּ֣מֶד אָרְכָּ֑הּ וַיַּחְגֹּ֤ר אוֹתָהּ֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לְמַדָּ֔יו עַ֖ל יֶ֥רֶךְ יְמִינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And made for himself Ehud a sword, and to it two mouths, a gomed its length, and he girded it under his garments on his right thigh.

en.L: And Ehud made for himself a sword; it had two mouths, a cubit [was] its length, and he girded it under his garments on his right thigh.
en.B: Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword, {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} long, and he strapped it to his right thigh under his clothes.
en.R: Ehud had made a sword for himself. It was sharp on both edges and {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} long. He tied it to his right thigh, under his clothes, where no one would see it.

decisions.choice: two mouths: two edges
decisions.reason: A blade's edge is called its "mouth", the part that "eats". With two edges, the sword could stab and cut.

decisions.choice: a gomed: a short length, probably a short cubit
decisions.reason: The word for the measure appears only here, not the usual word for cubit. It was probably a short cubit, perhaps measured from the elbow to the knuckles, so the blade may have been somewhat shorter than 18 inches. Either way it was a short sword that could be hidden.

decisions.choice: on his right thigh: where a left-handed man would draw from, and where no one would look
decisions.reason: A right-handed man wears his sword on the left thigh and draws it across his body. A left-handed man wears it on the right, so the weapon was in a place a guard would not expect, hidden under his clothes.

decisions.choice: had made
decisions.reason: The making of the sword happened before the visit to Eglon, so Balanced and Readable use "had made".

decisions.choice: where no one would see it
decisions.reason: Readable says why the sword was under his clothes, as the story implies.

source.text: וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וְעֶגְל֕וֹן אִ֥ישׁ בָּרִ֖יא מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought near the tribute to Eglon king of Moab; and Eglon [was] a man fat very.

en.L: And he brought the tribute near to Eglon king of Moab. And Eglon [was] a very fat man.
en.B: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was an extremely fat man.
en.R: Ehud brought the payment to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.

decisions.choice: fat: heavy, well-fed
decisions.reason: The word describes a well-fed body. It is used of fat cattle (Genesis 41:2) and of fattened animals (1 Kings 5:3). It prepares for verse 22.

decisions.choice: the visit may be told with words that suggest a sacrifice
decisions.reason: The name Eglon sounds like the word for a young bull, "brought near" is the verb used for presenting offerings, and the word for tribute also names an offering. The story may be picturing the king as a fattened animal brought to slaughter, but the text does not say so directly.

decisions.choice: Ehud
decisions.reason: Readable names Ehud where the Hebrew says "he".

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔ה לְהַקְרִ֖יב אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּנְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he had finished to bring near the tribute, and he sent away the people, carriers of the tribute.

en.L: And it was, when he had finished bringing the tribute near, that he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
en.B: When he had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried it.
en.R: After Ehud had given the payment, he sent away the people who had carried it.

decisions.choice: the people who carried the tribute: porters
decisions.reason: Tribute was paid in goods such as grain, animals, cloth and silver, so it took a group of people to carry it.

decisions.choice: he sent away: Ehud dismissed his own party
decisions.reason: Ehud is the subject. He goes with the porters part of the way home (verse 19) and then comes back alone.

decisions.choice: Ehud
decisions.reason: Readable names Ehud.

source.text: וְה֣וּא שָׁ֗ב מִן־הַפְּסִילִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת־הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דְּבַר־סֵ֥תֶר לִ֛י אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הָ֔ס וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו כָּל־הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he turned back from the carved images that [were] by Gilgal, and he said, a word of secret [is] to me for you, the king. And he said, hush! And went out from him all those standing by him.

en.L: But he himself turned back from the carved images that [were] at Gilgal and said, "I have a secret word for you, king." And he said, "Silence!" And all who were standing by him went out from him.
en.B: But Ehud himself turned back at the carved images near Gilgal and said, "Your Majesty, I have a secret message for you." The king said, "Quiet!" and all his attendants went out.
en.R: But at the carved images near Gilgal, Ehud turned around and went back. He said, "King Eglon, I have a secret message for you." The king said, "Quiet!" Then all his servants left the room.

decisions.choice: the carved images: carved stones or idols that marked a place near Gilgal
decisions.reason: The word usually means carved images, idols of stone or wood. Here they mark a place near Gilgal, where Israel set up twelve stones when it crossed the Jordan (Joshua 4:19-20); some take the word to mean those standing stones, or a stone quarry. Ehud passes them again in verse 26, so they may mark the edge of the land Moab controlled.

decisions.choice: a secret word: a private message, or a hidden thing
decisions.reason: The word for "word" can also mean "thing". Eglon hears a secret message, but what Ehud really has for him is the hidden sword. The same word returns in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the king said "Silence!": he ordered quiet until they were alone
decisions.reason: The king is the speaker. The word is a call for silence, so Ehud says nothing more until the attendants have gone.

decisions.choice: those standing by him: the king's attendants
decisions.reason: To "stand" before a king is to serve him (1 Kings 10:8). These are court servants on duty.

decisions.choice: king / Your Majesty / King Eglon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses him as "the king". Literal keeps "king"; Balanced uses the form of address English uses for a king; Readable uses his name.

decisions.choice: Ehud / the king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name each speaker, since the Hebrew says only "he".

source.text: וְאֵה֣וּד׀בָּ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהֽוּא־יֹ֠שֵׁב בַּעֲלִיַּ֨ת הַמְּקֵרָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵה֔וּד דְּבַר־אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֖קָם מֵעַ֥ל הַכִּסֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Ehud came to him, and he [was] sitting in [the] roof chamber of the coolness which [was] for him by himself. And said Ehud, a word of God [is] to me for you. And he rose from on the seat.

en.L: And Ehud came to him, and he [was] sitting in the roof chamber of coolness, which [was] his alone. And Ehud said, "I have a word of God for you." And he rose from on the seat.
en.B: Ehud came to him as he sat alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you," and the king rose from his seat.
en.R: The king was sitting by himself in his cool room upstairs. Ehud went up to him and said, "I have a message from God for you." When the king heard this, he stood up from his seat.

decisions.choice: the roof chamber of coolness: a room built on the roof, open to the breeze
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs, and a room could be built on top (1 Kings 17:19; 2 Kings 4:10). With openings for the wind, such a room was the coolest place in the building, which mattered in the heat of the Jordan valley.

decisions.choice: his alone: a private room
decisions.reason: The room was for the king's own use. No one would come in without being called, which explains the locked doors and the long wait in verses 23-25.

decisions.choice: a word of God: a message from God, or a thing from God
decisions.reason: The word for God can also mean "a god", so to Eglon it could sound like a message from a deity. Ehud means Israel's God, and, as in verse 19, the "word" he brings is also a "thing": the sword.

decisions.choice: he rose from the seat: the king stood up for the message
decisions.reason: Standing to receive a word from a god was a mark of respect. It also brought the king to his feet and within reach of Ehud. The word for seat can mean a throne.

decisions.choice: roof chamber / upper room / room upstairs
decisions.reason: Each level says where the room was in words its readers know; all three mean a room on the top of the house.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵהוּד֙ אֶת־יַ֣ד שְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־הַחֶ֔רֶב מֵעַ֖ל יֶ֣רֶךְ יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֶ֖הָ בְּבִטְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent out Ehud his left hand, and took the sword from on his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.

en.L: And Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the sword from on his right thigh and thrust it into his belly.
en.B: Ehud reached with his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into the king's belly.
en.R: Then Ehud used his left hand to pull the sword from his right thigh, and he pushed it into the king's stomach.

decisions.choice: left hand ... right thigh: the hand no one watched
decisions.reason: This brings together the details of verses 15-16. A guard watches a man's right hand and his left side; Ehud's weapon came from the other side.

decisions.choice: his belly: the king's
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Eglon.

decisions.choice: the king's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose belly, to avoid confusion with Ehud.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א גַֽם־הַנִּצָּ֜ב אַחַ֣ר הַלַּ֗הַב וַיִּסְגֹּ֤ר הַחֵ֨לֶב֙ בְּעַ֣ד הַלַּ֔הַב כִּ֣י לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ף הַחֶ֖רֶב מִבִּטְנ֑וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הַֽפַּרְשְׁדֹֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went in also the hilt after the blade, and closed the fat behind the blade, for not he drew the sword from his belly; and it went out toward the parshedon.

en.L: And the hilt also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and it came out [at] the back.
en.B: Even the handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because Ehud did not pull the sword out of his belly. And the point came out at his back.
en.R: Even the handle went in after the blade. The king's fat closed over it, because Ehud did not pull the sword out. And the point came out through his back.

decisions.choice: it came out at the back: the point of the blade came through
alternatives: and he went out into the back passage
decisions.reason: The last word appears only here, and its meaning is not certain. It has an ending that means "toward" a place, which suits the blade going through to the back. Others take it as the dung coming out of the body, which would explain the servants' guess in verse 24, or as Ehud going out through a back way, which verse 23 then tells more fully.

decisions.choice: he did not draw the sword out: Ehud left it in the body
decisions.reason: Ehud is the subject. The fat closed over the blade, and he left the sword where it was.

decisions.choice: the fat: the very fat king of verse 17
decisions.reason: The detail of verse 17 now pays off: the king's own fat swallows the sword.

decisions.choice: the point
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what came out, following the reading chosen in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֵה֖וּד הַֽמִּסְדְּר֑וֹנָה וַיִּסְגֹּ֞ר דַּלְת֧וֹת הָעַלִיָּ֛ה בַּעֲד֖וֹ וְנָעָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Ehud toward the misderon, and he shut [the] doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked.

en.L: And Ehud went out to the porch, and he shut the doors of the roof chamber behind him and locked [them].
en.B: Then Ehud went out into the porch. He shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
en.R: Then Ehud went out to the porch. He closed the doors of the room upstairs behind him and locked them.

decisions.choice: the porch: a passage or entrance hall outside the room
decisions.reason: This word too appears only here. It seems to name a hall, porch or row of columns leading out of the room. Some take it as an opening for a toilet through which Ehud slipped out.

decisions.choice: he shut the doors and locked them
decisions.reason: Doors could be locked with a wooden bolt that was worked by a key, from outside as well as inside (verse 25). The story does not say exactly how Ehud locked them and got away; the point is that the doors were found locked.

source.text: וְה֤וּא יָצָא֙ וַעֲבָדָ֣יו בָּ֔אוּ וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה נְעֻל֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אַ֣ךְ מֵסִ֥יךְ ה֛וּא אֶת־רַגְלָ֖יו בַּחֲדַ֥ר הַמְּקֵרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he had gone out, and his servants came, and they saw, and look, [the] doors of the roof chamber [were] locked. And they said, surely covering he [is] his feet in [the] room of the coolness.

en.L: And he had gone out, and his servants came and looked, and there, the doors of the roof chamber [were] locked. And they said, "Surely he [is] covering his feet in the room of coolness."
en.B: After Ehud had left, the king's servants came in and found the upper room's doors locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool room."
en.R: After Ehud left, the king's servants came. They saw that the doors of the room upstairs were locked. They said, "He must be using the toilet in his cool room."

decisions.choice: covering his feet: relieving himself
decisions.reason: This is a polite way of speaking about going to the toilet; the robe covered the feet as a man squatted. It is used the same way of Saul in 1 Samuel 24:4.

decisions.choice: his servants: the king's court attendants
decisions.reason: These are the officials who waited on the king, the same men he sent out in verse 19.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: The word for servant here means the king's court attendants, so every level says "servants" rather than "slaves", and none says "officials", since these men wait at his door.

decisions.choice: Ehud / the king's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Ehud and say whose servants these are, since the Hebrew says only "he" and "his".

source.text: וַיָּחִ֣ילוּ עַד־בּ֔וֹשׁ וְהְנֵּ֛האֵינֶ֥נּוּ פֹתֵ֖חַ דַּלְת֣וֹת הָֽעֲלִיָּ֑הוַיִּקְח֤וּ אֶת־הַמַּפְתֵּ֨חַ֙ וַיִּפְתָּ֔חוּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נֵיהֶ֔ם נֹפֵ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה מֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And they waited until shame, and look, there was not he opening [the] doors of the roof chamber; and they took the key and opened, and look, their lord fallen to the ground, dead.

en.L: And they waited until [they were] ashamed, and there, he was not opening the doors of the roof chamber. And they took the key and opened [them], and there [was] their lord, fallen to the ground, dead.
en.B: They waited until they were embarrassed, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and there was their master, lying dead on the floor.
en.R: They waited and waited until they felt foolish, but the king still did not open the doors. So they got the key and unlocked the doors. There was their master, lying dead on the floor!

decisions.choice: until shame: until they were embarrassed at how long they had waited
decisions.reason: The phrase means a very long time, to the point of embarrassment (2 Kings 2:17; 8:11). They did not want to disturb the king in private.

decisions.choice: the key: a wooden key that worked the bolt
decisions.reason: A key of this time was a piece of wood that reached through a hole in the door and lifted the pins that held the bolt, so a locked door could be opened from outside.

decisions.choice: their lord: a plural of rank for one master
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form, as is usual for a master of high rank, but means one person, the king.

decisions.choice: master
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lord"; Balanced and Readable say "master", since the servants are speaking of the king they serve, not of God.

source.text: וְאֵה֥וּד נִמְלַ֖ט עַ֣ד הִֽתְמַהְמְהָ֑ם וְהוּא֙ עָבַ֣ר אֶת־הַפְּסִילִ֔ים וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט הַשְּׂעִירָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Ehud escaped while they delayed, and he passed the carved images and escaped to Seirah.

en.L: And Ehud escaped while they delayed, and he passed beyond the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
en.B: Ehud got away while they were waiting. He passed the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
en.R: While they waited, Ehud got away. He went past the carved images near Gilgal and escaped to Seirah.

decisions.choice: the carved images: the same place as in verse 19
decisions.reason: Ehud passes the place where he turned back, now going the other way, toward safety.

decisions.choice: Seirah: an unknown place
decisions.reason: The place is not named anywhere else. The name sounds like a word for wooded or rough country, and the next verse puts Ehud in the hill country of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: near Gilgal
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader where the carved images were (verse 19).

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹא֔וֹ וַיִּתְקַ֥ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּרְד֨וּ עִמּ֧וֹ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִן־הָהָ֖ר וְה֥וּא לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he came, and he blew on the horn in [the] hill country of Ephraim, and went down with him [the] sons of Israel from the hill country, and he before them.

en.L: And it was, when he came, that he blew the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he [was] before them.
en.B: When he arrived, he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hills, with Ehud at their head.
en.R: When he got there, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim to call the people to battle. The Israelites came down from the hills with him, and he led the way.

decisions.choice: blew the trumpet: called the men to war
decisions.reason: The instrument was the shofar, a ram's horn (not a metal trumpet), blown as a signal to gather fighting men (6:34; 1 Samuel 13:3).

decisions.choice: the hill country of Ephraim: the central highlands
decisions.reason: This is the high ground west of the Jordan, in the middle of the land. From there the men "went down" toward the Jordan valley and Jericho.

decisions.choice: to call the people to battle
decisions.reason: Readable says why Ehud blew the trumpet. As in Joshua 6 and Judges 7, the shofar is "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and "ram's horn" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel / the Israelites
decisions.reason: These are the fighting men who answered the call, so no gender setting applies here.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ רִדְפ֣וּ אַחֲרַ֔י כִּֽי־נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־אֹיְבֵיכֶ֛ם אֶת־מוֹאָ֖ב בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אַחֲרָ֗יו וַֽיִּלְכְּד֞וּ אֶת־מַעְבְּר֤וֹת הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לְמוֹאָ֔ב וְלֹֽא־נָתְנ֥וּ אִ֖ישׁ לַעֲבֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, pursue after me, for has given Yahweh your enemies, Moab, into your hand. And they went down after him and captured the fords of the Jordan to Moab, and not they let a man to cross.

en.L: And he said to them, "Pursue after me, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." And they went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan toward Moab, and they did not let anyone cross.
en.B: He told them, "Follow me, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has handed your enemies the Moabites over to you." So they went down after him and took control of the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and they let no one cross.
en.R: He told them, "Follow me! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given you victory over your enemies, the Moabites." So they followed him down and took control of the shallow places where people crossed the Jordan River to Moab. They did not let anyone cross.

decisions.choice: has given: the victory is as good as done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act. Ehud speaks of the battle that has not yet been fought as already won by the LORD (4:7, 14; 7:15).

decisions.choice: pursue after me: follow me into battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to chase. Ehud calls the men to follow him and chase the enemy.

decisions.choice: the fords of the Jordan toward Moab: the crossings that led home to Moab
decisions.reason: The Moabite troops were west of the Jordan, around Jericho. By holding the shallow crossings, Israel cut off their way back to Moab on the east side.

decisions.choice: has given you victory over
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture "given into your hand".

source.text: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֶת־מוֹאָ֜ב בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא כַּעֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֔ישׁ כָּל־שָׁמֵ֖ן וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ חָ֑יִל וְלֹ֥א נִמְלַ֖ט אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they struck Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, every stout and every man of strength, and not escaped a man.

en.L: And they struck Moab at that time, about 10,000 men, every one stout and every one a man of strength, and not a man escaped.
en.B: At that time they struck down about 10,000 Moabites, all of them sturdy and able fighters; not one got away.
en.R: At that time they killed about 10,000 Moabite soldiers. All of them were strong, well-fed fighting men, but not one of them escaped.

decisions.choice: stout: well-fed, robust
decisions.reason: The word means fat or sturdy. It echoes the very fat king of verse 17: like their king, the sturdy men of Moab fell.

decisions.choice: men of strength: capable fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase names able, strong men fit for war.

decisions.choice: about ten thousand
decisions.reason: The word for "thousand" is the one discussed at Numbers 1, where the size of such figures is noted. "About" shows the number is given as a round figure.

decisions.choice: Moabite soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that these were Moab's fighting men.

source.text: וַתִּכָּנַ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא תַּ֖חַת יַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֖רֶץ שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was subdued Moab on that day under [the] hand of Israel, and was quiet the land eighty years.

en.L: And Moab was subdued on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land was quiet eighty years.
en.B: So Moab was brought under Israel's power on that day, and the land had peace for eighty years.
en.R: That day Moab was defeated and came under Israel's control. Then the land had peace for eighty years.

decisions.choice: subdued under the hand of Israel: brought under Israel's power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The oppressor is now the one held down.

decisions.choice: eighty years: twice forty, the longest rest in the book
decisions.reason: Othniel's rest was forty years (verse 11); this one is two generations.

decisions.choice: had peace
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

source.text: וְאַחֲרָ֤יו הָיָה֙ שַׁמְגַּ֣ר בֶּן־עֲנָ֔ת וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ שֵֽׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ בְּמַלְמַ֖ד הַבָּקָ֑ר וַיֹּ֥שַׁע גַּם־ה֖וּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck [the] Philistines, six hundred men, with [the] goad of the cattle, and delivered also he Israel.

en.L: And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck [the] Philistines, 600 men, with a cattle goad; and he too delivered Israel.
en.B: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. He struck down 600 Philistines with an ox goad, and he too rescued Israel.
en.R: After Ehud there was Shamgar son of Anath. He killed 600 Philistines with a long, pointed stick used for driving oxen. He also rescued Israel.

decisions.choice: Shamgar son of Anath
decisions.reason: Anath is the name of a Canaanite war goddess. "Son of Anath" may name his father, his home town (perhaps Beth-anath, 1:33), or a title for a warrior. Shamgar is named again in 5:6.

decisions.choice: a cattle goad: a farmer's long pointed stick
decisions.reason: A goad was a long wooden pole, often with a metal point, used to drive oxen at the plow. A farm tool became a weapon; later the Philistines kept iron tools out of Israel's hands (1 Samuel 13:19-22).

decisions.choice: he too delivered Israel: Shamgar is counted with the deliverers
decisions.reason: No cycle of sin, oppression and cry is told for Shamgar, and no years are given, but he is named as another rescuer God used, like Othniel and Ehud.

decisions.choice: a long, pointed stick used for driving oxen
decisions.reason: Readable explains "goad", which most readers will not know.
